title: Coding Challenge 2: Inheritance
description: Learn the principle of Inheritance in Object-Oriented Programming. Inheritance allows a child class to inherit properties and methods from a parent class. Create an 'Animal' base class with a 'run()' method. Then create a 'Human' class that extends Animal, adding a 'name' property and overriding the run() method to return a specific message.
requirements: Create an 'Animal' base class with a 'run()' method
Create a 'Human' class that extends Animal
The Animal's run() method should return 'Animal is running'
Human's constructor should accept and store a 'name' parameter
Human's run() method should return '[name] is running' (overriding parent method)
Use 'super()' to properly initialize the parent class
hints: Use 'extends' keyword to create a subclass
Use 'super()' in the constructor to call parent constructor
You can override parent methods by redefining them in the child class
Call super() before using 'this' in child constructor
The parent's run() method is still accessible if needed

tests.name: Animal class exists
tests.test: function() { try { const a = new Animal(); return typeof a === 'object' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Animal is not a class' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Animal has run() method
tests.test: function() { try { const a = new Animal(); return typeof a.run === 'function' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Animal does not have run() method' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Animal run() returns correct message
tests.test: function() { try { const a = new Animal(); const result = a.run(); return result === 'Animal is running' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Animal is running", got "' + result + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Human class extends Animal
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('John'); return h instanceof Animal ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Human does not extend Animal' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Human has name property
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('Alice'); return h.name === 'Alice' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Human name property not set' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Human run() is overridden
tests.test: function() { try { const h = new Human('Bob'); const result = h.run(); return result === 'Bob is running' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Expected "Bob is running", got "' + result + '"' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }

tests.name: Both classes work independently
tests.test: function() { try { const a = new Animal(); const h = new Human('Charlie'); return a.run() === 'Animal is running' && h.run() === 'Charlie is running' ? { success: true } : { success: false, message: 'Classes not working independently' }; } catch(e) { return { success: false, message: e.message }; } }
